item.vignette: A 13-year-old boy has persistent Epstein-Barr virus viremia, recurrent lymphadenopathy, and reduced cytotoxic activity of natural killer cells. Flow cytometry shows markedly decreased NKG2D on NK cells and CD8+ T cells. Sequencing identifies a loss-of-function variant in MAGT1. Immunoblotting of patient lymphocytes shows underglycosylated NKG2D protein with reduced steady-state expression.
item.lead_in: Which cellular process is most directly impaired by this mutation?

options.A: N-linked glycosylation of selected proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum
options.B: O-linked glycosylation of proteins in the Golgi apparatus
options.C: TAP-dependent transport of cytosolic peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum
options.D: Proteasomal degradation of ubiquitinated cytosolic proteins
options.E: Attachment of glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchors to proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum

item.tested_construct: MAGT1 deficiency causes selective defects in N-linked glycosylation, including hypoglycosylation and reduced expression of NKG2D
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: MAGT1 participates in the oligosaccharyltransferase machinery that supports N-linked glycosylation of selected proteins. In MAGT1 deficiency, NKG2D becomes hypoglycosylated and its steady-state surface expression falls, impairing cytotoxic lymphocyte function and contributing to susceptibility to persistent EBV infection.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. MAGT1 deficiency can impair N-linked glycosylation of selected proteins; NKG2D hypoglycosylation directly explains its reduced steady-state expression in the vignette.
distractor_explanations.B: O-linked glycosylation occurs primarily in the Golgi and is not the defect demonstrated for NKG2D in MAGT1 deficiency.
distractor_explanations.C: TAP transports peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum for MHC class I loading; loss causes an antigen-presentation defect rather than selective NKG2D hypoglycosylation.
distractor_explanations.D: The ubiquitin-proteasome system degrades cytosolic proteins and does not account for the observed glycosylation defect.
distractor_explanations.E: GPI-anchor attachment is a distinct endoplasmic-reticulum modification and does not explain selective underglycosylation of NKG2D in MAGT1 deficiency.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize MAGT1 deficiency as a selective N-linked glycosylation disorder in which NKG2D hypoglycosylation reduces NKG2D expression and compromises cytotoxic lymphocyte function.

item.vignette: A 27-year-old man has recurrent episodes of confusion after carbohydrate-rich meals. During an episode, plasma ammonia and citrulline are markedly elevated. He has a longstanding preference for protein- and fat-rich foods. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC25A13.
item.lead_in: Which mitochondrial transport process is most directly impaired?

options.A: Import of ornithine from the cytosol into the mitochondrial matrix
options.B: Export of aspartate from the mitochondrial matrix in exchange for glutamate plus a proton
options.C: Export of carbamoyl phosphate from the mitochondrial matrix into the cytosol
options.D: Import of pyruvate from the cytosol into the mitochondrial matrix
options.E: Export of acetyl-CoA directly across the inner mitochondrial membrane

item.tested_construct: Citrin is the mitochondrial aspartate-glutamate carrier that exports aspartate to the cytosol while importing glutamate plus a proton
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: SLC25A13 encodes citrin, a calcium-regulated aspartate-glutamate carrier in the inner mitochondrial membrane. Citrin exports mitochondrial aspartate to the cytosol while importing glutamate with a proton. Cytosolic aspartate is required for argininosuccinate synthesis in the urea cycle, and citrin is also a component of the malate-aspartate shuttle; loss therefore can produce hyperammonemia and citrullinemia.

distractor_explanations.A: Mitochondrial ornithine import is mediated by the ornithine transporter and is defective in HHH syndrome, not citrin deficiency.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. Citrin exchanges mitochondrial aspartate for cytosolic glutamate plus a proton across the inner mitochondrial membrane.
distractor_explanations.C: Carbamoyl phosphate is generated and used within the mitochondrial portion of the urea cycle; its export is not the defining SLC25A13 transport step.
distractor_explanations.D: Mitochondrial pyruvate import is mediated by the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier, not citrin.
distractor_explanations.E: Acetyl-CoA does not cross the inner mitochondrial membrane directly; carbon units are exported through shuttle systems such as citrate.

explanation.educational_objective: Link SLC25A13/citrin deficiency to loss of mitochondrial aspartate export, impaired malate-aspartate shuttling, and reduced cytosolic aspartate availability for the urea cycle.

item.vignette: A newborn develops recurrent seizures that persist despite phenobarbital and levetiracetam but stop after intravenous pyridoxine. Urine and plasma contain markedly increased alpha-aminoadipic semialdehyde and piperideine-6-carboxylate. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in ALDH7A1.
item.lead_in: Which biochemical mechanism most directly explains the pyridoxine dependence?

options.A: Failure to oxidize pyridoxine phosphate to pyridoxal 5-prime-phosphate because of PNPO deficiency
options.B: Competitive inhibition of glutamate decarboxylase by accumulated alpha-ketoglutarate
options.C: Condensation of accumulated piperideine-6-carboxylate with pyridoxal 5-prime-phosphate, functionally inactivating the cofactor
options.D: Failure of intestinal vitamin B6 absorption because of loss of a sodium-dependent pyridoxine transporter
options.E: Accelerated renal excretion of pyridoxal 5-prime-phosphate caused by proximal tubular dysfunction

item.tested_construct: ALDH7A1 deficiency causes P6C accumulation, which chemically condenses with and inactivates pyridoxal 5-prime-phosphate
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: ALDH7A1 encodes alpha-aminoadipic semialdehyde dehydrogenase in lysine degradation. Deficiency causes accumulation of alpha-aminoadipic semialdehyde and its cyclic form, piperideine-6-carboxylate (P6C). P6C chemically condenses with pyridoxal 5-prime-phosphate (PLP), the active vitamin B6 cofactor, producing functional PLP deficiency and pyridoxine-responsive seizures.

distractor_explanations.A: PNPO deficiency can also cause vitamin B6-responsive neonatal epilepsy, but this patient has the characteristic ALDH7A1 biomarker pattern; the mechanism is PLP sequestration by P6C rather than impaired PNPO conversion.
distractor_explanations.B: Alpha-ketoglutarate accumulation is not the defining biochemical lesion in ALDH7A1 deficiency and does not explain the characteristic P6C-mediated loss of PLP.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. Accumulated P6C condenses with PLP and inactivates this vitamin B6 cofactor, producing pyridoxine dependence.
distractor_explanations.D: ALDH7A1 deficiency is a lysine-catabolism disorder, not a defect of intestinal pyridoxine absorption.
distractor_explanations.E: The disorder does not primarily result from renal PLP loss; the active cofactor is chemically inactivated by an accumulating lysine metabolite.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy due to ALDH7A1 deficiency as a lysine-catabolism disorder in which accumulated P6C chemically inactivates PLP.

item.vignette: A 5-month-old infant has poor growth, chronic diarrhea, recurrent Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, and megaloblastic anemia with pancytopenia. Serum folate and cerebrospinal-fluid 5-methyltetrahydrofolate are both very low, whereas vitamin B12 is normal. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC46A1.
item.lead_in: Which transport defect most directly explains both the systemic and neurologic folate deficiency?

options.A: Loss of folate receptor-alpha-mediated uptake at the choroid plexus with preserved intestinal folate absorption
options.B: Loss of intrinsic-factor-dependent cobalamin uptake in the terminal ileum
options.C: Loss of the reduced folate carrier that mediates folate entry into systemic tissues at near-neutral pH
options.D: Loss of proton-coupled folate transport across the apical proximal small intestine and at the choroid plexus
options.E: Loss of intracellular folylpolyglutamate synthesis that normally retains folates within cells

item.tested_construct: SLC46A1 encodes the proton-coupled folate transporter required for intestinal folate absorption and for folate transport into cerebrospinal fluid
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: SLC46A1 encodes the proton-coupled folate transporter (PCFT). PCFT is highly expressed on the apical membrane of the proximal small intestine, where it mediates dietary folate absorption, and it also participates in folate transport at the choroid plexus. Loss therefore causes both systemic folate deficiency with megaloblastic cytopenias and severe cerebral folate deficiency.

distractor_explanations.A: FOLR1 loss impairs folate transport into cerebrospinal fluid but typically leaves serum folate and the hemogram relatively preserved; it does not explain combined intestinal malabsorption and cerebral deficiency.
distractor_explanations.B: Intrinsic factor mediates vitamin B12 absorption, not folate transport; this patient has normal vitamin B12.
distractor_explanations.C: The reduced folate carrier is important for folate transport into many systemic cells, but SLC46A1 encodes PCFT, the transporter required for intestinal absorption and choroid-plexus folate transport.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. PCFT mediates proton-coupled folate uptake in the proximal intestine and contributes to folate transport into cerebrospinal fluid.
distractor_explanations.E: Folylpolyglutamate synthesis retains folates intracellularly after uptake and does not explain the characteristic intestinal and choroid-plexus transport defect.

explanation.educational_objective: Distinguish hereditary folate malabsorption from isolated cerebral folate disorders by recognizing that SLC46A1/PCFT is required for both proximal-intestinal folate absorption and transport of folate into cerebrospinal fluid.

item.vignette: A 10-month-old boy develops lethargy and tachypnea during a viral illness. Laboratory studies show hyperammonemia, lactic acidosis, hypoglycemia, and urinary metabolites suggesting impaired activity of several mitochondrial carboxylases. Biotinidase activity is normal. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in CA5A, which encodes mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase VA.
item.lead_in: Which molecule is normally generated by the deficient enzyme to support the affected mitochondrial pathways?
item.tested_construct: Mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase VA generates bicarbonate that is supplied to CPS1 and multiple mitochondrial carboxylases
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Carbonic anhydrase VA catalyzes mitochondrial hydration of carbon dioxide to bicarbonate. The locally generated bicarbonate is required by carbamoyl phosphate synthetase 1 in the urea cycle and by mitochondrial biotin-dependent carboxylases including pyruvate carboxylase, propionyl-CoA carboxylase, and 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase. CA5A deficiency can therefore produce simultaneous hyperammonemia, lactic acidosis, hypoglycemia, and a multiple-carboxylase biochemical pattern.

distractor_explanations.A: NADPH is not the product generated by mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase VA and is not the common substrate defect linking CPS1 with the affected carboxylases.
distractor_explanations.B: Biotin is a cofactor for the mitochondrial carboxylases but not for CPS1, and carbonic anhydrase VA does not synthesize biotin.
distractor_explanations.C: N-acetylglutamate activates CPS1 but is not required by pyruvate, propionyl-CoA, or 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylases and is not generated by carbonic anhydrase.
distractor_explanations.D: Tetrahydrofolate participates in one-carbon metabolism and is not the molecule supplied by carbonic anhydrase VA to these mitochondrial enzymes.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. Carbonic anhydrase VA generates intramitochondrial bicarbonate used by CPS1 and several bicarbonate-dependent carboxylases.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize CA5A deficiency as impaired mitochondrial bicarbonate generation, simultaneously compromising CPS1 and several biotin-dependent carboxylases.
